references.text: Solomon's proverbs teach that a person's pride leads to humiliation, while the humble gain honor: 'Pride goes before destruction, and a haughty spirit before a fall' (Proverbs 29:23). This is the same principle Jesus states in Luke 14:11.
The Proverbs warn that 'pride comes before destruction, and a haughty spirit before a fall' (Proverbs 16:18), which reflects Jesus' words that whoever exalts themselves will be humbled.
'The fear of the Lord is instruction in wisdom, and humility comes before honor' (Proverbs 15:33). The principle that humility leads to exaltation underlies Jesus' statement.
'Before destruction a man's heart is haughty, but humility goes before honor' (Proverbs 18:12). A direct parallel to Jesus' words that whoever humbles themselves will be exalted.
Job 22:29 speaks of God saving those who lower their eyes in humility, reflecting the principle that whoever humbles themselves will be exalted by God.
Through the prophet Ezekiel, God speaks of making the low high and the high low (Ezekiel 21:26), a principle concerning God's right to humble the proud and exalt the humble.
Jesus repeats exactly the same statement in Matthew 23:12: 'Whoever exalts themselves will be humbled, and whoever humbles themselves will be exalted.' This is a direct parallel.

In the parable of the Pharisee and the tax collector, Jesus repeats the same principle in Luke 18:14: 'For everyone who exalts themselves will be humbled, but whoever humbles themselves will be exalted.'

Jesus teaches his disciples that 'whoever makes themselves like this child is the greatest in the kingdom of heaven' (Matthew 18:4), a concrete illustration of the principle that humility leads to exaltation.
James writes that 'God opposes the proud but gives grace to the humble' (James 4:6), which supports Jesus' teaching that the humble are exalted by God.
'Humble yourselves before the Lord, and he will lift you up' (James 4:10). A direct exhortation based on the same principle Jesus formulates.

Peter exhorts: 'Clothe yourselves with humility toward one another ... Humble yourselves therefore under the mighty hand of God so that at the proper time he may exalt you' (1 Peter 5:5-6). The same principle as in Luke 14:11.

Isaiah prophesies that 'the lofty looks of man shall be humbled, and the haughtiness of men shall be bowed down, and the Lord alone shall be exalted in that day' (Isaiah 2:11-12). God's judgment on the proud points to the same principle.
